company_profile: Bolt is a European mobility platform for ride-hailing, delivery and rentals, automating operational decisions such as support, document checks and fraud review.
title: Applied AI Engineer
summary: Senior AI Engineer with 8+ years shipping and operating ML and LLM systems in production across Healthcare, Telecom and AIOps, with an MSc in Machine Learning and AI. Builds evaluation pipelines with LLM evaluators, agent tracing and failure detection, and knows when classical ML such as LightGBM or XGBoost is the better tool. Fine-tunes open models when prompting is not enough and works in SQL on real operational data. Alongside this, I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD.

project.name: Support Refund Decision Agent
bullets: Built an LLM agent that decided customer support refund cases for a mobility marketplace, calling order-history and policy tools, with a LightGBM model handling routine cases more cheaply.
Evaluated it on test sets built from past human decisions, calibrated an LLM judge against human labels, and served it through FastAPI behind an A/B-tested rollout gate.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Applied AI Engineer role in Operations Automation at Bolt. I have shipped and operated LLM systems at United Health Group and Viavi, and the part I care about most is the unglamorous loop around them: test sets, traces, and working out why an agent got a decision wrong.

Bolt's plan to rebuild support, document checks and fraud review around decisions that improve with every case is the work I want to be doing, on-site next to the people who run those processes. My fiancée lives in Berlin, and we plan to move to Tallinn together and settle there long term.

I would start where the role does, with evaluation. I built evaluation and observability pipelines for our Question Answering and Summary Agents, with LLM evaluators and tracing, that cut human review by 43%. I also run a lab-extraction agent with Claude and Amazon Textract across about 1,800 documents, and at Viavi I let LightGBM do the prediction and GPT-3.5 only the explaining.

Outside work I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD. It has taught me to judge a system by what it does for the teacher using it, not by a benchmark. I would welcome a conversation about the role.
